title: When Is a Relevance Threshold Statistically Resolvable? Minimax Limits for Effect Classification
summary: Statistical precision and scientific relevance operate on different scales. In regular problems, sampling uncertainty contracts at rate $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the magnitude below which an effect is scientifically negligible may be fixed or may vary with information. Let $Δ_n$ denote a relevance threshold and $I_0$ Fisher information, and define $λ_n=\sqrt{nI_0}Δ_n$. For separated negligible and meaningful parameter classes, we establish the minimax lower bound $\liminf R_n^*\ge 2\{1-Φ(\varepsilonκ)\}$ when $λ_n\toκ$.
